name: All That for a Hand Crack?
text: [approach] Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp.
[descent_text] After the second pitch, mantel above the anchor onto the snow, which leads to the descent line.
[descent_text] Walk off to the south over the snow, the same way as for the other routes on the west face.

name: Granitic Dreams
text: [overview] Length varies with snowpack: about 230 feet in June, with the first anchors near 140 feet, and at least 30-40 feet longer after summer melt.
[approach] Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp.
[descent_text] Walk off to the south over the snow, the same way as the other west face routes.
[descent_text] Rappelling this line is a poor idea because it is long, and snowmelt over the season lengthens it further.

name: Kuriositeten
text: [overview] Three solid water ice pitches with snow and alpine ice between them.
[overview] A vertical snow and ice chimney opens the route, followed by steep snow (about 60 m) to the second pitch, AI3-4 ice up to the gully's central snow bowl.
[overview] Roughly four or five simul-climbed rope lengths then lead to the best ice: about 60 m of WI5 easing to WI3 near the top, then several lengths of steep snow to the ridge.
[overview] The less glaciated back side allows a fairly easy descent to the pass.
[approach] Camps on the glacier floor put the base within a short approach.
[descent_text] Parties who topped out chose not to reverse the couloir, because the snow flank at its top faces southeast and softens as the day warms.

name: Mt. Michelson - North Ridge
text: [overview] this line climbs the ridge on the north side, lying between the two northern glaciers.
[overview] Esetuk Creek is followed beyond many forks over wet tundra, then rock, talus and boulder slopes holding snow into June;
[overview] Cross Esetuk Glacier close to the toe, climb steeper boulders to the ridge, then mostly snow steepening to about 45 degrees.
[overview] Early-season snow may be loose, with deep postholing.
[detailed_rack] Pickets are possible later in the season, once the snow is consolidated.
[approach] The ground is wet tundra giving way to talus and boulder slopes where snow lingers into June, and the travel is slow and tedious.
[approach] Go over the Esetuk Glacier close to its terminus to get to the root of the peak, then work up a steep boulder field to a higher point on the ridge, where the terrain turns to snow.

name: Skunk
text: [overview] Climb 70-80 degree steps interspersed with gentler ramps for about 80 feet to the alders, then weave through them and tunnel up steep, sometimes deep snow, perhaps tying off alders for protection.

name: Dragonfly Jr.
text: [overview] P2: climb up and right to steeper sustained ice for 50 m until it eases, then 13 m of gentle ice and snow lead to a big ice chunk on the right, a comfortable belay spot.
[approach] Leave a vehicle at the plowed pullout beside the Parks Highway, on its west side, and ski or snowmachine up Cantwell Creek to the boundary of the Denali wilderness.
[approach] Snowmachines are left at the boundary;
[approach] The climb is on an east-northeast-facing wall, partly hidden by a spine coming off the rocky face south of the glacier.
[approach] Skirt the big snow bowl to reach the foot of the ice.
[approach] The Cantwell Glacier above can shed seracs onto the route, and rockfall potential is above average.

name: Didilkama Traverse
text: [overview] Beyond, descend toward the next tower and follow the ridge to the Snowbird Glacier, where route finding, rappels or hard downclimbing may be needed.

name: East Ridge
text: [overview] Approach from Ptarmigan Creek or mile 27 (in spring and summer the pipeline road goes part way up), or from the trailhead at Worthington Glacier and up that glacier.
[overview] Winter and spring give a wild ridge of cornices, rime and fifth-class steps;
[overview] in summer it is largely 3rd class rock with a few patches of snow and some 5th class climbing.
[overview] From the 27 Mile Glacier, access matches the South Ridge, then take the obvious couloir to the col.
[overview] Alternatively ascend the Worthington Glacier for 3 miles.
[overview] Descending the East Ridge and escaping down Worthington Glacier is a good choice if the sunny side warms up.
[detailed_rack] Crampons, ice axe and glacier equipment, with a small set of fine pitons and nuts.

name: Northwest Couloir
text: [overview] A steep snow couloir;
[overview] ski or snowboard descents typically rappel to get in.
[detailed_rack] Steep snow in highly complex avalanche terrain;
[approach] The terrain is steep snow and very complex avalanche terrain, so check the local avalanche forecast first.

name: Rhinestone Wizard
text: [overview] climb it only when snowfall has been light or the hazard is low.
[overview] P4 (WI4/5): mushroomed pillar or curtain to a snow stance at the bottom of a big basin.
[overview] Afterward, cross snow toward the upper left to reach the ridge and walk west, or thread and reverse the approach.
[approach] The route is on the south face of Tiehacker Mountain, up Glacier Creek above Seward.
[descent_text] Descend by V-thread rappels, or climb snow up to the ridge on Tiehacker and follow the summer trail down to the Bear Lake neighborhood.

name: Goldfinger
text: [overview] good weather and dry conditions are hard to catch (snow near the summit, storms and water on pitch 3 turned parties back).
[overview] After lots of snowfall, start left of the main corner on easy ground to a ledge, after steep snow with a hidden moat (belay it).

name: South Gully/Ridge
text: [overview] A wide snow couloir at 40-50 degrees, bending slightly right, runs for 1800 feet before it constricts, forks and kicks up.
[overview] The right fork rises several hundred feet more and may hold some combination of ice, snow and rock, possibly with moderate ice or mixed climbing.
[overview] a brief snow traverse at low angle leads to the next couloir, which turns left onto the south ridge.
[overview] The ridge is easy 4th class with gendarme bypasses to a snowfield summit.
[overview] The couloir funnels debris, so move quickly and early and watch snow conditions.
[detailed_rack] Natural gear, slung horns and perhaps a picket or two.

name: Toe gully
text: [overview] Tools and crampons are optional.
[approach] Follow the first fault line up to the basin of the Cleveland Glacier, then continue up the basin to the obvious cliff band.

name: Gunnison
text: [overview] P2 (200 ft): steep snow.
[overview] P6 (100 ft): through the cornice to the rim.

name: Great White Conqueror
text: [overview] Snow and ice, steep, make up the lower half.
[detailed_rack] Add a picket or two and 4-6 screws.
[approach] Parties reach the Mendenhall Towers by a short helicopter flight from Juneau, or on skis from the ridge north of the Mendenhall Glacier to its north branch, or directly up the glacier.
[approach] For this line on the north face of the West Tower, follow the snow as high as possible and then trend left onto the face.

name: North Face
text: [overview] best in winter or spring, when the two main approaches are easier with snow cover.
[overview] The first goes up steep snow to a 30 ft rock band, then more snow with boulders suitable for sling anchors.
[overview] With the band snowed over it felt about 5.7 / M2+, and good gear turned up after digging.
[overview] The second is 55-degree snow up to the boulder on top (5.4, easier on the back side).
[detailed_rack] A picket or two is optional.

name: Morning Salutes
text: [overview] Locate the two prominent, unmistakable rock pillars on the ridge, then go up, crossing the bergschrund and following a moderate snowy ramp into the rock band.
[overview] After gaining the crest, head west, placing pickets as seems wise.
[detailed_rack] Compact alpine rack: two or three cams to 2 in, four nuts, one or two ice screws, one or two pickets, and a 60 m or 70 m rope.

name: Gank'd and Slayed
text: [overview] Start at the foot of the snow cone, where the northwest face's three main routes meet;
[overview] Corners trending right, then a steep snow traverse, lead to a belay.
[overview] a small cornice had to be chopped.
[overview] Judge the avalanche hazard on the hugely exposed snowfield above.
[overview] They crossed more than one rope length of snow with no protection, dug a snow cave for a second bivy, then climbed one WI3 pitch.
[descent_text] After topping out on the 6,000-foot subpeak northeast of the true summit, parties hiked over it and descended the Icicle Glacier by the standard northeast ridge route.

name: Mountaineer's Route
text: [overview] From the glacier, take a brief gully facing right to the bench under the snowfield, skirt the snowfield's right side, then follow the first ledge system that leads leftward above it.

name: Mt. Michelson, South Face
text: [overview] The southern side departs from the glacier of that name, covers 1000-2000' of loose blocks, talus and snow, and then follows a final line of snow and ice up to the crest of the summit ridge.
[detailed_rack] A few pickets and ice screws may help.

name: Col of the Wild
text: [overview] brief cruxes of ice or mixed rock appear now and then, with much simulclimbing on steep snow.
[overview] Near the top a large cornice may need tunneling.
[detailed_rack] Standard alpine rack: some small and medium cams, a nut selection, knifeblades, angles, screws for ice, specters and a few pickets.

name: North Face
text: [overview] Cross a bergschrund after moderate snow to reach the rock.

name: North Troll Couloir
text: [overview] Climb the 60 degree snow couloir, steep and west facing, between the North and Middle Trolls, up to the point right under the col.
[detailed_rack] A standard rack plus snow gear.

name: Northeast Ridge
text: [approach] Approach North Troll via the glacier from the landing strip.

name: Northwest Ridge
text: [approach] Little Switzerland is reached by flying to the Pika Glacier, where the base camp sits.

name: Kissing up the choss pile
text: [approach] From the Reed Lakes lot, walk to the former building site, short of Nugget Boulder and the Snowbird slab.
[approach] Then take the path bearing left up the drainage, past the Snowbird mine on your right, and keep going up the bowls to the pass.
[approach] The Snowbird Glacier lies below the pass, and the Nunatak is the small formation beside it.

name: Thunderbolt (Lightening Bolt) Couloir
text: [overview] Steep snow couloir, also a steep to extreme Chugach Front Range ski line, harder than Ptarmigan North.
[what_to_bring] crampons — advisable (boot and ski).
[what_to_bring] ice axe or ice tool — or at least a whippet

name: Mixed Inhibitions
text: [overview] P2 (M7, 25 m) climbs a very steep crack that trends left in a corner facing left, then neve and a runnel to a snow ledge.
[approach] the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark.

name: S (north) couloir, The
text: [detailed_rack] Snow pickets, or a running belay if judged necessary.
